questions: Should the random_state for train_test_split and RandomForestClassifier be fixed (e.g., 42) or left unspecified (potentially non-deterministic)?
If the CSV contains non-numeric feature columns, should they be automatically encoded (e.g., one-hot) or should the function raise an error?
Should the classification report use default sklearn metrics (e.g., digits=2) or some other precision?
If the target column contains strings (e.g., 'cat', 'dog'), should the report's class ordering be alphabetical, by appearance, or by sklearn's default?
Should missing values (NaN) in the CSV be handled (e.g., dropped, imputed) or left to pandas/sklearn default (which may raise an error)?

Is the function required to work for multi-class classification only, or also binary? (The formatting clarification mentions 5 parts for class lines, which matches multi-class; binary reports may have fewer.)
Should the function ensure the target column has at least two classes? What if all samples belong to one class?
Are there any constraints on the CSV file size or number of features? Should the function handle large datasets efficiently?
